parsed.explanation: The division itself is strongly protective: gender-identity nondiscrimination and hate-crime law, a care shield, open M/F/X documents, and custody rules respecting gender identity. Its local facilities are not under a birth-sex ban. But the shared national framework still governs every visitor’s border crossing and immigration custody: passport/visa sex-marker restrictions, suspicion-based refusal and possible lifetime fraud findings, invasive screening, and documented abuse in immigration detention. Existing X-marker passports remain valid and courts have blocked some measures, so this is not severe-risk territory. The local protections are real but cannot override the national border and custody exposures, so the jurisdiction remains at elevated risk rather than reduced risk.
